title: Null-byte regression test comment is factually wrong
description: mime-tree/src/decode.rs test_uuencode_null_byte_in_encoded_payload_no_panic says: 'wrapping_sub(32) & 0x3F treats 0x00 as value 0 (same as 0x60/backtick or 0x20/space)'. This is wrong. In uuencoding/src/decode_line(), data bytes go through decode_byte() which rejects anything not in 0x20..=0x5F or 0x60. A 0x00 byte in data position returns Err(InvalidChar), not value 0. wrapping_sub(32) is used only for the length byte (line[0]). The test still passes because 'no panic' is the actual invariant — the invalid char triggers Err which causes is_truncated=true, not a panic. The comment just misexplains the mechanism. Fix: rewrite comment to say 0x00 in the data payload triggers InvalidChar from decode_byte(), causing is_truncated=true with empty data — the key invariant being no panic regardless of the error path taken.
close_reason: Fixed: rewrote comment to correctly describe the 0x00 → Err(InvalidChar) → is_truncated=true path; removed the incorrect wrapping_sub reference.
